That's only 12 words. The words "next turn" are currently redundant
but a limit of 12 instead of 10 is fine. It's tight enough to make
the questions simple as you wanted.

And there's another approach. A question like this is not a valid
yes/no question as the only sensible answer is "maybe". I'm not sure
what the actual Monocle text is, but the online text goes wrong with

"If the question pertains to the future, he or she must abide by the

answer if possible". The future is hypothetical and uncertain and so
one cannot ask valid yes/no questions about it. If you bar this
nonsense then I doubt that you need a word limit.

The consequence would be that useful questions could only be about
cards that the target player can see but the acting player cannot,
i.e. cards in hand, inactive vampires and the contents of the Storage
Annex. One might allow questions about deck contents too, provided
deck lists are available to refresh a player's memory.

In a friendly game, one might also allow questions about a player's
state of mind, e.g. "do you plan to bleed me next turn?" but the
answers are subject to change, impossible to verify and so this can
only be played using the honour principle.

You prove my point. I'll have to do your work for you. From what has
been said, the broken question would be of the form:

---------------------------------------------------------------------
Is this statement true: "(You will bleed me next turn and your answer
will be NO) or (You will not bleed me next turn and your answer will
be YES)"?
---------------------------------------------------------------------

This has the desired effect - an answer of YES means that "You will
not bleed me next turn" must be true, while an answer of NO means that
"You will bleed me next turn" must be false. Either way, the player
cannot bleed.

But this question is trivial to strike down. Pick any or all of the
following grounds:

1. It is not a direct question about the game.

2. It is, in effect, two questions not one - will you bleed me and
what will your answer be?

3. It is self-referential - "a question about questions".

4. It is too complex. Even if this is written down and studied, a
player could fairly answer "I don't know". It demands a clear head
and a grasp of boolean logic and these are not mandatory requirements
for competitors.

5. It is a trick question and so could be ruled unsporting.

And that's just using the existing rules. If you used either of my
suggestions - using a word limit or forbidding questions about the
future - then the question would be invalid on both of these grounds
too.

Of course, it should never come to this. Any player whipping out an
index card and reciting something like this should first be told,
"don't be silly - ask a proper question".

Andrew

We're entering the realms of fantasy here. But supposing that there
were ever a VTES tournament with a prize purse this large, the Monocle
would be the least of your problems. Your real problem would be
dealing with the inevitable collusion and bribery. See
rec.gambling.poker for details of what to expect.

You get these problems as it is with Magic but VTES would be more
vulnerable because it is a multi-player game and its format already
encourages players to split tables. Once you have a large fungible
prize then you're no longer playing for VPs or to win - you're playing
for a slice of the cake instead. I recall a long thread on rgtcm in
which Ryan Dancey said that FRPG would never run a serious big
tournament using a multi-player format because collusion would be rife
and suspicion would poison the atmosphere. He had a point.

An additional problem is that the VEKN rules are one-size-fits-all.
It seems that many players will only consider playing the game using
the VEKN tournament rules. Banning the Monocle from all levels of
play because of an occasional big money tournament is making the tail
wag the dog. The big money tournaments are rare or non-existent and
so should have their own house rules to suit their special
circumstances. It would be like the levels of enforcement that you
get in Magic.

Andrew
